terms.grammar: adjective used as a noun (neuter plural of omnis)
evidence: Cic. Sen. 21: omnia quae cūrant meminērunt
terms.comment: Latin says “all things”, in the plural: ut sint omnia parāta, have everything ready (Cic. Fam. 14.20.1). “Everything else” is cētera.

evidence: Ov. Met. 15.177–178: nihil est tōtō, quod perstet, in orbe. cūncta fluunt
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: all in a body, all together, the whole.

phrases.latin: in Tusculānum nōs ventūrōs putāmus aut Nōnīs aut postrīdiē. ibi ut sint omnia parāta
phrases.english: we expect to reach Tusculum on the Nones or the day after. Have everything ready there
drop everything and look after your health
they remember everything they care about

sources: Lewis & Short: omnis · Lewis & Short: cunctus · Lewis & Short: ceterus
